Dear Parents, Carers and Visitors,
A warm welcome to Holy Apostles’ Church of England Primary School. We hope you can get a sense of the vibrant spirit, ambitious pursuits, and nurturing environment that define our school. Holy Apostles’ is located on the south western edge of Cheltenham with a fantastic view of the Cotswold escapement.
At Holy Apostles’ Church of England Primary School, we take pride in our rich tradition, firmly grounded in the school's Christian ethos and vision. This tradition ensures that our pupils are well-behaved but also learn to care for themselves and each other. Guided by our dedicated staff, they are empowered to achieve high standards across all aspects of their school life.
Being a Church of England Primary School, we cherish our close ties with Holy Apostles’ Church. Reverend Collishaw regularly joins us for school worship, enhancing the sense of community and spiritual growth.
Our overarching goal is to ensure that all pupils, whenever they leave us, are sufficiently equipped with the skills and resilience needed to triumph over the challenges that await them. We place immense importance on our partnerships with parents, the Church, and the community to achieve this objective. Visitors often highlight the joyful and industrious atmosphere we foster, qualities we actively cherish and promote. Within our school community, every member, from children to parents/carers, staff, and beyond, is acknowledged and celebrated for their contribution to the success of Holy Apostles’ School. Our purpose is to inspire each child to cultivate a profound love for learning, offering them a diverse range of opportunities. In essence, "Learn Well, Live Well, Together" encapsulates our school’s way of life, permeating everything we do and grounded in our Christian values.
We, the staff and governors, are proud of our school and the personal and academic achievements of our pupils. Hopefully you will find the answers to many of your questions on this site. If you are interested in finding out more, do get in touch. Our children and staff would love to show you around.
We look forward to meeting and working with you so that Holy Apostles’ School continues to be the very special place that it is.
Total points for the year so far: Matthew - 604 Mark - 639 Luke - 695 John - 755
If you have a child who will be entering primary school in September 2027, we would like to welcome you to visit our school. Visits will commence at 9.30am and 1.30pm and will last for approximately 1 hour on the following dates:-
Wednesday 4th November 2026
Wednesday 6th January 2027
To book onto one of the above visits please email admin@holyapostles.gloucs.sch.uk
Please include a contact telephone number in your email, thank you.
We look forward to meeting you soon.
Dan SmithHeadteacher

British Values
British Values
Promoting British Values at Holy Apostles’ Primary School
The Department of Education (DfE) directs schools to promote the fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. At Holy Apostles’ these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy is highly valued at the school. We consider it important that children have opportunities for their voices to be heard. We have a School Council whose members are voted in by their class (one boy and one girl), the Head Teacher and the Deputy Head Teacher. Council members meet regularly to discuss issues raised in their class. Pupil questionnaires and pupil voice meetings also provide opportunities for views to be put forward.
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, is consistently reinforced throughout the school day as well as when dealing with behavioural issues and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws that govern and protect us, the responsibilities that these involve and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Local MP, Mayor, Police and Fire Service etc. are part of our calendar and help to reinforce this message.
Our pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for our pupils to make choices safely, through the provision of a safe environment and wide range of learning opportunities. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advised how to exercise these safely through, for example, our E-Safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it be through choice of challenge, recording work, participating in our extra-curricular clubs and other opportunities, our pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Holy Apostles’ serves a multi-faith community where each person is respected and valued equally regardless of ability, gender, faith, heritage or race. Cultural appreciation and development forms part of our curriculum. We place great emphasis on providing opportunities for pupils to participate in events and celebrations to broaden their experiences and awareness of others. Our assemblies help all pupils to find out about themselves and others linking their lives to the communities to which they belong.

About Us
Holy Apostles’ is a Voluntary Aided Church of England Primary School which was provided by Charles Cooke-Higgs in 1873 as part of the Foundation and Endowment of Holy Apostles’ Church. In July 1966, on the first centenary of Holy Apostles’ Church, the foundation stone of the present school was laid and, following three further stages of development, the completed school was blessed and dedicated by the Right Reverend Jeremy Walsh, Bishop of Tewkesbury, in May 1993.
Central to the education which we offer is the provision of Christian Religious Education and a daily act of worship for all pupils – in keeping with the school’s Church of England Foundation. A majority of the Governing Body membership is appointed by the Foundation and serves, in particular, to appoint staff and admit pupils.
Holy Apostles’ School is situated close to the centre of Cheltenham in a pleasant residential area on the edge of the Battledown estate and caters for pupils aged 4 to 11. There are seven bright, spacious class rooms, main hall, a well-stocked library and ICT suite, grouped around a central garden. The school is generally well equipped; enjoys a safe outdoor play area and a large field which provide ideal settings for sports and social events; and, although no pupil currently on the school roll is physically disabled, wheelchair access to the main school entrance is possible.

Our Distinctive Christian Vision
Our school, in the context of our wonderful surroundings and closeness to the natural world, excels at doing what it does in a mutually supportive and caring environment, which brings together children across year groups, along with parents, carers, and staff, in a desire to work, not only for individual success, but for each other’s benefit too. In the classroom, on the sports pitch, on the stage, and beyond the school gates we desire together to see everyone flourish and reach their full potential. Our goal is that we all;
Learn Well, Live Well, Together
This vision is rooted in the Christian belief that every human being is created in the image of God, and that each is invited to work together with others and God to bring life and allow all of creation to flourish and grow.
‘God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them.
When considering this in school we use the following visual cues;
As all are equally made as the image of God and equally valued and precious, no child should be left behind. We will therefore aim to develop in each child:
Just as our Christian vision is the foundation of all we do at Holy Apostles, the opportunity to experience spirituality is woven into the heart of our curriculum planning and the wider experiences we provide.
We put great importance on developing relationships with others, both within school, our local community and the global community. We recognise the importance of a feeling of belonging, of being part of something bigger than the self.
Developing an awareness of a sense of self, of our uniqueness and developing language for recognising and describing emotions and feelings is a key part of our CPSHE curriculum. In addition, we look for opportunities to encourage a relationship with the natural world and this is often linked to providing opportunities to experience moments of stillness and reflection as well as of awe and wonder.
We aim to develop in each child:
Our collective worship centres around our core Christian Values of;
Love, Forgiveness, Happiness, Friendship, Equality, Honesty and Perseverance
We want to encourage our pupils to go out into the world as advocates of these values. Please visit our Key Information and Policies page for our RE and Collective Worship policies.

Governor Pen Portraits
I have been a parent at Holy Apostles since 2013, with my third son currently in Year three. All three of my children joined as pre-schoolers and I have been actively involved as a parent since then. I was Chair of the Pavilion Group for eight years, during which time I became a member of the Governing Body which I joined in 2014 as a Foundation Governor. I took on the role of Vice-Chair in 2022 before being elected as Chair in September 2023.
I have a background in secondary school teaching having been a PE teacher; a role which I thoroughly enjoyed before starting my family. I am passionate about education and believe in the importance of our children getting the best possible start in life in a setting that provides a safe, secure and happy environment alongside the delivery of their education to the highest possible standards.
Outside of this, I have a Health and Wellness business and I am currently undertaking my Yoga Teacher Training.
I have worked at Holy Apostles' as Class Teacher since 2006. Before that I taught in Staffordshire and worked on their Leading Literacy Team. My BA degree is in English and Education. During my years at Holy Apostles’ I have been involved with many art and drama projects and have been on the PTA for the last ten years. I am currently subject leader for R.E. I love Holy Apostles’ School and am deeply committed to continuing to ensure that all children know their value and uniqueness.
I have 2 grown up daughters and my hobbies include gardening, cooking and reading.
I joined the Holy Apostles’ governing body in Autumn 2025, hoping to contribute to and support the school where I can. It’s a lovely school, with excellent leaders, teachers and support staff, all working hard within tight budget constraints to deliver the best for our children.
I work in marketing and advertising, bringing experience in strategy and problem-solving. My aim is to offer practical support where it adds value, helping the school continue to provide a positive and well-rounded experience for all pupils.
My eldest son started at Holy Apostles’ Primary school in 1991, followed by his brother in 1993. Initially I joined the PTA, then in 1996 was elected as a parent governor. I became a Foundation Governor in 1998 and from 2001-2022 held the office of Chair. I retired from leading Holy Apostles’ Pre-school in 2023.
As a Foundation Governor and a member of Holy Apostles church, I am committed to ensuring that our Christian vision continues to be central to the teaching here. I am the RE subject Governor and I work closely with Ashley Collishaw, vicar at Holy Apostles, together with the subject lead. I also sit on Curriculum & Standards and Personnel committees.
As you can see, I have an enduring, passionate interest in Holy Apostles’ and I am committed to helping to create a thriving, happy environment where all can be the best they can be!
I have been a member of the Holy Apostles congregation since the early noughties and was elected to their Parochial Church Council in 2023. I am committed to ensuring that our Christian vision continues to be central to the teaching here at Holy Apostles School and work closely with Ashley Collishaw the Vicar at Holy Apostles. I also sit on the School’s Finance & Premises committee. I have a business background combined with academia with an MBA and DipM from Oxford Brookes and am a qualified Chartered Marketer and Fellow of the CIM, Member of the IScT and Member of the AMBA for over 30 years and am or have been a Director of over 20 Limited Companies for over 25 years.
I feel privileged to be able to support Holy Apostles' Church of England Primary School as a Parent Governor. I have a daughter who attends the school and she thoroughly enjoys being part of the school community, both in her academic learning and in the social and creative opportunities that she experiences.
I currently work as a Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator at another primary school in the county and I have a particular interest in the social and emotional development of children.
I aim to work closely with the school governing body, where individuals come together to share ideas and expertise, to support the school community to continue to be the successful team that it is.
I have been Vicar of Holy Apostles Church in Charlton Kings since 2019, and am married to Alex with three children currently moving through the different stages of A levels and University. I have been ordained now for around twenty years, and based in Cheltenham for fifteen of those. I am a lifelong supporter of Nottingham Forest and enjoy watching sport, films, playing a little golf (badly), and occasionally “dabbling in oils.”
Originally from the north-west I moved to Cheltenham in 2007 following three years in America coaching football and skiing to primary school aged children. From a professional perspective my current role, which I have been in for over fifteen years is teaching and coaching in an FE college where I am also responsible for leading improvements in teaching and learning. In additional to a PGCE and various coaching qualifications I have acquired a Masters in Educational Leadership and have a keen interest in supporting improvements in learning along with most sports and music. I live locally and with my wife Emma and two children who both attend Holy Apostles.
I formally joined the governing body in March 2025. I have a B.Ed and an M.Ed from the University of Bristol. Prior to that I worked for Hambros Bank in the city and labouring for a firm in Aldershot.
I taught in middle and primary schools and also the university of the West of England. I’ve been head of two primary schools.
I worked for the local authority as an adviser , a senior adviser and then Head of School Improvement. I led inspections for Ofsted and was employed as an improvement adviser for the National Strategies.
I was involved in the development of Diocese of Gloucester Academies Trust, writing guidance and policy documentation, and undertaking school audits.
I have been a parent at Holy Apostles’ since 2019, with a son who has long since departed for secondary school and a daughter who is currently enjoying all that the school has to offer in terms of academic, music and sporting activities. I have been a Foundation governor since October 2025 and I also sit on the Curriculum & Standards Committee. As a governor I am especially interested in ensuring the school continues to develop its Christian Vision, and that it does all it can to foster a safe, welcoming, inclusive environment in which children can flourish.
As a family we have been involved with Holy Apostles church for many years, with both my wife and I taking separate stints on the Parochial Church Council and also supporting youth work there. My background is in cyber security and information technology and I work in business development for a software development company. I enjoy cooking, running and chasing round after our energetic spaniel!
